result.mechanism: A 25-year Built-Own-Operate-Transfer project worth about Rs 138 crore, won by an associate company in which Krystal holds 49%. The concession sits in the associate, not in Krystal's consolidated revenue.
result.rationale: The trigger is a Rs 138 crore, 25-year BOOT project won by an associate in which Krystal holds 49%: the stated total is 10.4% of TTM revenue, but Krystal's share is about Rs 2.7 crore a year and the associate is not consolidated, so it belongs mostly to someone else (fatal flaw: share too small to matter). Krystal wins Rs 100-370 crore contracts several times a year, so the flow is routine, and the thin-margin and cheap-valuation exception does not rescue a 49%-owned associate's concession. The Rs 364 crore Tamil Nadu contract of March 2026 is only a comparable in this packet and should be triaged separately.

result.mechanism: Three municipal solid waste management (sanitation) contracts from Vasai Virar City Municipal Corporation (VVCMC), a government body, worth about Rs 275 crore in total over five years plus a three-month preparatory phase. The company supplies the service and is paid as it executes, so the contracts add operating revenue over the five-year period.
result.rationale: Size: Rs 275 crore total over five years is 21.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,295.96 crore, about 4% a year. Firm: work orders from VVCMC (a government body) are received for Rs 83 crore and Rs 111 crore, with the third contract implied. Routine by pattern: the company regularly wins contracts of this size (Rs 370 crore, Rs 349 crore, Rs 168 crore in 2025), so routine=true, but the TTM operating margin of 6.5% and market cap of 0.67x TTM revenue trigger the exception, and TTM revenue growth of +18.0% is above zero, so it is decided as non-routine. No disqualifier: the company is rated A-/Stable and the work is a first large municipal SWM award.
result.what_changed: A large municipal solid waste contract is the company's first big civic (municipal) SWM award in the packet. Earlier SWM and water-treatment wins in 2025 were described as pre-qualification for larger projects. The Rs 275 crore total is 21.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,295.96 crore but spans five years, so it is about 4% of revenue per year. The company also wins many large contracts (Rs 370 crore Sep 2025, Rs 349 crore May 2025), so the order is routine by pattern, and the cheap-valuation and thin-margin exception applies.
contradictions: TTM operating margin is 6.5%, thin and flat on a year earlier, so the margin benefit of the new contracts is unproven
Five-year contract value gives about 4% of revenue per year, against 21.2% headline
result.next_milestone: Start of the three-month preparatory phase and mobilisation of the VVCMC contracts; Q3 FY26 results showing the order's contribution and the margin on the new municipal work.

Krystal Integrated Services Limited Secures ₹65 Crore Facility Management Contract from MSEDCL

● To oversee O&M of key power substations across Maharashtra for three years Mumbai, August 05, 2025: Krystal Integrated Services Limited (KISL), a leading provider of integrated facility management solutions, has been awarded a significant work order from the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL).

The contract, valued at approximately ₹65 crore (excluding taxes and duties) for a period of three years, encompasses the provision of Facility Management Services (FMS) and allied services, including the Operation & Maintenance (O&M) of 33/11 kV, 33/22 kV, and 22/11 kV substations or switching stations across the state.
